findings.title: Blocked-email matching can be bypassed with case variants
findings.body: This lookup compares the submitted address exactly with the stored address, and the registration validation path does not canonicalize it first. Since email domains are case-insensitive, a blocklist entry for `bad@example.com` will not match `bad@EXAMPLE.COM`, allowing the latter to pass validation and register. Normalize stored and submitted addresses consistently, or use a case-insensitive comparison.

findings.title: Validation side effects double-count blocked signup attempts
findings.body: Calling `should_block?` increments the stored match statistics during model validation. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` and then calls `user.save`, which validates again; a single blocked signup attempt therefore increments `match_count` twice. Keep statistics tracking out of validation or ensure it runs once per signup attempt.

findings.title: Concurrent matches can lose counter increments
findings.body: This read-modify-save sequence is not atomic. If two blocked signup validations load the same `match_count` before either saves, both can write the same incremented value, so the final count increases by one instead of two. Use an atomic database increment (and update `last_match_at` atomically) to preserve the statistics under concurrent requests.
